questions.question: Who requested the Syrian king to send a Greek philosopher?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindusara** was the second Mauryan emperor of India.
 
• Bindusara ruled from approximately **297 BCE to 273 BCE**.
 
• He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the father of Ashoka.
 
• Bindusara requested the Syrian king Antiochus I to send a Greek philosopher to his court.
 
• This request indicates the cultural and intellectual exchanges between the Mauryan Empire and the Hellenistic world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• He founded the Maurya Empire in ancient India, he established a centralized state and united most of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He ruled from **321 to 297 BCE **and was advised by the strategist **Kautilya**, also known as **Chanakya**.
 
• His reign marked the beginning of one of India’s largest empires.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka:**
 
 
• Grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, he ruled the Maurya Empire from **268 to 232 BCE **and is renowned for his promotion of **Buddhism and non-violence**.
 
• After witnessing the devastation of the **Kalinga War**, he embraced and propagated moral and ethical governance.
 
• His edicts, inscribed on pillars and rocks, reflect his commitment to justice and welfare.

questions.question: In the mid - eighth century, Dantidurga, a Rashtrakuta chief, overthrew his Chalukya overlord and performed a ritual literally called a ______.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Golden Womb:-**

 
 
• It​ is a ritual performed by ancient Indian rulers to ensure the** birth of a son** who would be the rightful heir to the throne.
 
• This ritual involved the king lying down on a **bed of gold** and his queen sitting on his lap.
 
• The queen would then be blessed by the priests to** conceive a male child.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsidiary alliance:-**

 
 
• It was a treaty between an Indian state and the British East India Company, under which the Indian state would provide the Company with troops and money in exchange for protection from external attack.
 
• The Indian state would also be required to accept a British Resident at its court, who would advise the ruler on all matters of foreign policy.

questions.question: The Purva Mimansa school of philosophy was founded by __________ in ancient India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaimini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Purva Mimansa school of philosophy** traces its origins back to Jaimini, who founded it in ancient India **around 400 B.C.**.
 
• **Jaimini** is renowned as the author of the Mimansa Sutra, a seminal text in Hindu philosophy.
 
• This school of thought, Purva Mimansa, places significant emphasis on the importance of yajnas (ritual sacrifices) and mantras (sacred utterances) in upholding the cosmic order.
 
• It asserts that human salvation can only be achieved by adhering to the principles laid down in the Vedas. Mimamsa is classified as one of the six orthodox schools of Indian philosophy, alongside Nyaya-vaisheshika systems.
 
• It underscores the significance of valid knowledge and holds that the Vedas are timeless repositories of all knowledge. According to Mimamsa philosophy, religion entails fulfilling the duties prescribed by the Vedas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Krishna Dvaipayana**, commonly known as Vyasa or Vedavyasa, is a revered sage in various Hindu traditions, prominently recognized as the author of the epic Mahābhārata.
 
• **Kapila, **also known as Cakradhanus, is another esteemed sage in Hindu lore. According to the Bhagavata Purana, he is the son of the sage Kardama and Devahuti, who was the daughter of Svayambhuva Manu and the sister of Mahasati Ansuya.
 
• **Patanjali, **alternatively referred to as Gonardiya or Gonikaputra, is renowned as a Hindu author, mystic, and philosopher. Although the exact timeframe of his life remains uncertain, estimates based on the analysis of his works suggest that he may have lived between the 2nd century BCE and the 4th century CE.

questions.question: Rudradaman belonged to which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Rudradaman I :

__
 
• He is considered the greatest of the Saka rulers.
 
• He is from the Western Kshatrapa dynasty.
 
• He was the grandson of Chastana.
 
• His kingdom included Konkan, Narmada valley, Kathiawar, other parts of Gujarat, and Malwa.
 
• He conducted the repair work of the Sudarshana Lake at Kathiawar. 
 
• He supported Sanskrit literature and cultural arts.
 
• It was during Rudradaman’s reign that Yavaneshwara, the Greek writer lived in India and translated the Yavanajataka from Greek to Sanskrit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kushans were one of the five Great Yueh-chi tribes.

 
 
• The Great Yuezhi-Chi tribes dwelled in the valley of Oxus.
 
• A century later the Kushans of Yuehi-Chi gained dominance over the others.
 
• They were led by Kadphises.
 
• In the 1st century CE, Kujula Kadphises (Kadphises I) brought these five tribes together and founded the Kushan Empire.
 
• They are referred to as Guishuang in the Chinese sources.
 
• They moved east towards India by defeating the Parthians and the Sakas in the 1st century AD.
 
• Kujula Kadphises was the first Yuezhi chief to lay the establishment of the Kushana Empire in India.
 
 
• He substantiated his supremacy over Kabul, Kandahar and Afghanistan.
 
• His successor was his son Vima Taktu or Sadashkana (AD 80 -AD 95) who amplified the empire into northwest India.
 
 
 
• Ruler Vima Kadphises was the son of Vima Taktu and the father of Kanishka.
 
• Kanishka of Kushan Dynasty (127 AD – 150 AD)
 
 
• Kanishka was by far the most powerful sovereign of the Kushana dynasty.
 
• His capital was Purushpura (Peshawar).
 
• During his rule, the Kushana Empire expanded from Uzbekistan, Tajikistan to Mathura and Kashmir. 
 
• It was during his reign that Buddhism got divided into Mahayana and Hinayana.
 
• He founded the Shaka Era of A.D. 78.
 
• Kanishka patronized Buddhism and organized the 4th Buddhist council in the Kundalvana of Kashmir in 78 AD.
 
• The scholars in Kanishka’s court included Vasumitra, Asvaghosa, Nagarjun, Charaka and Parsva.
 
• Kanishka battled against King Han Ho-ti, the king of the Han dynasty of China.
 
 
• Kanishka defeated him in the second attempt.
 
 
 
• He invaded Patliputra and took the Buddhist monk Asvaghosa to Purushpura.
 
 
• Ashvoghosha is considered to be the first Sanskrit dramatist.
 
 
 
• The Kushana dynasty's decline commenced after his death.
 
 
 
• Kanishka was succeeded by his son Vasishka.
 
• Vasishka was succeeded by Huvishka and Kanishka II (son of Vasishka).
 
• Kanishka II was succeeded by Vasudeva I.
 
• Vasudeva I was the last great ruler of the Kushanas.
 
• After his death, the empire disintegrated.

__
 
• The following land classifications are mentioned in the Chola inscriptions:

 
 

 **devdan**
 Land granted to temples and religious institutions.
 
 

 **Shalbhogh**
 **Land granted for maintenance of schools.**
 
 

 **Brahmadeya**
 A type of land granted to Brahmins or priests.
 
 

 **Vellanavagai**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Chola Dynasty:

 
• One of the longest dynasties to rule the **southern parts of India is the Chola (8th-12th century CE).**
 
• It was founded by Vijayalaya.
 
• He defeated the Pallavas in the 9th century, and his reign officially began. Until the 13th century, this rule was in force for more than five centuries.
 
• In this dynasty, **Rajaraja Chola** was one of the most powerful rulers.
 
 
• He was the first person to visit the banks of the river Ganges.
 
• He got fame as the** conqueror of Ganges.**
 
• This period is known as the Golden Age of Cholas.
 
 
 
• Chola temples like Brihadeswara Temple, Rajarajeswara Temple and Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple took the Dravidian style of architecture to new heights.
 
• Nataraja in Tandava dance posture is an important example of Chola sculpture.
 
• **Chola Inscriptions:**

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest dated forts in India, as first mentioned in Alexander the Great's war records, bringing it to the 4th century BCE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kangra Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kangra Fort** is considered one of the oldest forts in India, with its origins dating back to the **4th century BCE**.
 
• The fort was mentioned in the war records of **Alexander the Great**, indicating its historical significance during his invasion of India.
 
• Located in **Kangra, Himachal Pradesh**, the fort stands as an emblem of the **Trigarta Kingdom**, which was one of the oldest kingdoms in India.
 
• The fort has witnessed numerous invasions, including attacks by **Mahmud of Ghazni** in the 11th century and **Feroz Shah Tughlaq** in the 14th century.
 
• Its strategic location near the confluence of the **Banganga and Manjhi Rivers** made it a critical stronghold in ancient and medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trigarta Kingdom:**

 
 
• An ancient kingdom mentioned in the Mahabharata, it was known for its warrior clans and strategic location in the Himalayan region.
 
• The Kangra Fort was the capital of this kingdom, serving as a vital center of power.
 
 
 
• **Alexander’s Invasion of India:**
 
 
• Alexander the Great invaded India in 326 BCE, and his records provide valuable historical insights into the Indian subcontinent during that era.
 
• The mention of Kangra Fort in his war records highlights its prominence even during ancient times.
 
 
 
• **Architecture of Kangra Fort:**
 
 
• The fort is renowned for its massive stone walls and intricate gateways, showcasing ancient Indian military architecture.
 
• It houses temples and palaces, including the **Ambika Devi Temple**, reflecting its cultural and religious significance.
 
 
 
• **Other Ancient Forts in India:**
 
 
• **Gwalior Fort:** Known for its historical importance and architectural brilliance, but built later around the 6th century CE.
 
• **Kumbhalgarh Fort:** Constructed in the 15th century by Rana Kumbha in Rajasthan, famous for its massive walls.
 
• **Mehrangarh Fort:** Built in 1459 by Rao Jodha in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, it is one of the largest forts in India.

questions.question: In which year did the last king of Punjab Maharaja Duleep Singh ascend on the throne of Punjab **at 10 years of age**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1849**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **year 1849, the last king of Punjab Maharaja Duleep Singh ascends the throne of Punjab at 10 years of age**.

 
 
• After the close of the **Second Anglo-Sikh War** and the subsequent annexation of Punjab on 29 March 1849, he was deposed at the age of ten and was put into the care of Dr. John Login and sent from Lahore to Fatehgarh on 21 December 1849, with tight restrictions on who he was allowed to meet.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** eighth son of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and that too from a minor wife, Duleep Singh became Maharaja of Punjab when he was just five years old**.

 
 
• But within six years, his kingdom, the sole independent power in mid-19th century north India, was defeated twice in battle by the British and annexed, he had to hand over the world's most famous diamond and spent the rest of his life in overseas exile.
 
 
 
• Duleep Singh never abandoned hope of regaining his kingdom - though his efforts were subverted by the British, managed to hit back at them - especially over the Kohinoor - and his memory endures in both India and Britain in some curious ways, says British historian Peter Bance, author of half a dozen books on Sikh history in Britain.
 
 
• These include **"The Duleep Singh's: The Photograph Album of Queen Victoria's Maharajah", and "Sovereign, Squire & Rebel: Maharajah Duleep Singh and the heirs of a Lost Kingdom"**.
